brief: GS's daily wrap frames the tape as a battle between positive Iran headlines and a yield spike: the 10yr jumped to 5.19%, its biggest one-day rise since liberation day, while the S&P held roughly flat (+12.5% ytd) and GS's High Beta Momentum basket extended an 8-day win streak. A Tehran headline hinting at a return to the nuclear MOU before elections helped sentiment, but Iran's parliament speaker publicly threatened a return to 1970s-style oil/gas conditions and diesel shortages if the standoff continues. Separately, Xi and Trump met again: the trade truce was extended two months with a new joint trade arrangement, and Xi raised Taiwan, mutual-defense restraint, AI safety, and support for a US-Iran MOU. Trump's team is separately weighing a 90-day diesel export ban despite producer warnings it would raise future fuel prices (already $6.52/gallon vs $2.83 a year ago). On AI capex: GS raised Micron estimates on DRAM/HBM4 tightness, Oracle sent Blue Owl a force-majeure notice on its Project Jupiter data center after an 8% intraday drop, and GS flagged hyperscalers need ~$300bn in AI revenue to break even on 2026-27 capex as realized ROIC has fallen from 40% to 25%, while still forecasting 11% S&P EPS growth in 2027-28.

cards.claim: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.19%, its biggest one-day increase since the 'liberation day' tariff shock.
cards.anchor: US 10yr at 5.19% with the biggest daily increase since liberation day

cards.claim: The S&P 500 was roughly flat, down 2bps at 7704 (+12.5% year-to-date), caught between positive Iran headlines and a higher-yield backdrop.
cards.anchor: S&P -2bps @7704 (+12.5% ytd) on “positive Iran headlines vs higher yield” battle

cards.claim: Goldman's High Beta Momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) gained another 1.3% and has now risen for 8 consecutive days.
cards.anchor: our High Beta Momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) gained another +1.3% and is now up 8 days in a row

cards.claim: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran would push the US back toward 1970s-era conditions with higher gas prices and diesel shortages if the confrontation continues.
cards.anchor: We’ll return you to 1970s rates, plus high gas prices, diesel shortages and bell-bottoms

cards.claim: A headline that Tehran hopes the US returns to the nuclear memorandum of understanding before elections helped lift the market yesterday.

cards.claim: During the Xi-Trump meeting, Xi expressed support for the US and Iran returning to the memorandum of understanding and maintaining talks.
cards.anchor: Xi supports US and Iran to return to MOU and maintain talks

cards.claim: The Xi-Trump meeting extended the US-China trade truce by two months, with both sides agreeing to a new joint arrangement on trade.
cards.anchor: trade truce extended for 2 months; both sides agreed on a new joint arrangement on trade

cards.claim: Xinhua reported that Xi wants the US to insist it opposes Taiwan independence.
cards.anchor: Xinhua news mentioned Xi hope US to insist "oppose Taiwan independence"

cards.anchor: Xi mentioned US and China should not set up defences against each other, and should have dialogue

cards.claim: Xi said the two countries should prevent AI from being abused and ensure human control of AI.
cards.anchor: prevent AI being abused and ensure human control of AI

cards.anchor: Oracle (lost -3.5%yday, was even -8%)

cards.claim: Goldman's US equity strategist estimates hyperscalers need roughly $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their average annual capex investments in 2026 and 2027.
cards.anchor: generate annual AI revenues of roughly $300 billion in the next few years to break even on their average annual capex investments in 2026

cards.claim: Realized hyperscaler return on invested capital has declined from 40% to 25%.
cards.anchor: Realized hyperscaler return on invested capital has declined from 40% to 25%

cards.claim: Goldman forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 11% in both 2027 (to $415) and 2028 (to $460), driven partly by solid GDP growth.
cards.anchor: we forecast EPS growth of 11% in both 2027 (to $415) and 2028 ($460), driven by solid GDP growth

cards.claim: Goldman expects the EPS growth driver mix to shift as a fading AI investment tailwind gradually transitions into a growing boost from AI productivity.
cards.anchor: a fading tailwind from AI investment that gradually transitions into a growing boost from AI productivity
